q: Echoes are produced where a sound wave is ____ from a large and hard surface.
e: Echoes come from reflection at a large hard surface. An echo is a repetition of the original sound. Soft rugs and carpets absorb instead of reflecting.

q: An echo is ____ of sound due to the reflection of sound.
e: Echoes follow the laws of reflection: angle in equals angle out. A large hard wall sends a countable repeat; many walls make reverberation. A reflection grating uses shiny grooves instead of openings.

q: The echo or the reflected sound can be heard separately from the original sound if the source of the sound is much closer to the observer than to the ____ surface.
e: Reflection sends a wave back from a boundary, with angle in equal to angle out. A large hard wall gives a countable echo. Soft padding absorbs instead of bouncing.

q: Reflection of sound obeys the laws of ____.
e: Echoes follow the laws of reflection: angle in equals angle out. A large hard wall sends a countable repeat; many walls make reverberation. A reflection grating uses shiny grooves instead of openings. Stiffer media generally carry it faster.

q: To reduce the effect of echo in buildings, walls are covered up with padding and the floors are covered with rugs and ____.
e: An echo is a delayed repeat after reflection from a large hard surface. Soft padding absorbs instead of bouncing. Range follows from the go-and-return time, v = 2d/t.

q: Echo can also be used to determine the ____ between a source of sound and the reflecting surface.
e: fs is the frequency the source emits; vs is how fast the source moves through the still medium. Source toward the observer raises pitch; source away lowers it. v without a subscript is the wave speed in the medium.

q: Some animals such as bats are known to use ____ to navigate and locate their prey.
e: Echolocation means emitting sounds and reading the returning echoes. Bats navigate and hunt that way. Sonar is the engineered version in water.

q: A ____ is a reflection of light or sound waves, or a wide reaching impact of an action.
e: Reverberation is a wash of many reflections, as sound bouncing around a large hall. It is not absorption, and it is not a single delayed echo you can count. Padding cuts reverberation by eating the bounces.
